question: How can a Christian finish well?
answer: Hebrews tells us to "strip off every burden, and the sin that wraps itself around us so readily, and let us run the race laid out ahead of us, and run it with endurance" (Hebrews 12:1), keeping our eyes on Jesus. Faithfulness at the finish line grows out of faithfulness in the thousand small choices of ordinary days, as Polycarp's eighty-six years of service show. Above all, perseverance is first God holding on to us: "Until you are old I am He, and until your hair turns gray I am the one who will carry you" (Isaiah 46:4).

question: Can older or sick believers still bear fruit for God?
answer: Yes. The psalm promises that the righteous "Even when they are old they will still bear fruit; they will stay rich with sap and green" (Psalm 92:14). The fruit may look different: prayer instead of preaching, wisdom instead of labour, patience instead of activity. "Our outer self may be decaying, but our inner self is being made new day after day" (2 Corinthians 4:16).

question: What does it mean to leave a spiritual legacy?
answer: It means passing the faith on, like a baton in a relay race: "what you heard from me before many witnesses, pass on to trustworthy people who will be able to teach others as well" (2 Timothy 2:2). The faith passed from the apostle John to Polycarp to Irenaeus and onwards to us. Most of us will not leave money or famous books, but we can leave a faith that has been seen, tested and shared with children, younger believers and neighbours.
